audience.text: Python developers building applications that require generating Code 128, Code 39, EAN-13, EAN-8, UPC-A, UPC-E, and QR Code barcodes without system-level dependencies.

capabilities.text: Supports Code 128, Code 39 (base and Extended), EAN-13, EAN-8, UPC-A, UPC-E, and QR Code (Model 2) through dedicated helpers and `generate()`.
capabilities.title: Generate multiple barcode symbologies

capabilities.text: Produce SVG via `to_svg()` returning a string, and PNG via `to_png()` returning bytes; both accept optional `RenderOptions`.
capabilities.title: Render barcodes to SVG and PNG

capabilities.text: Control scale, DPI, module width/height, quiet zone, colors, and text display via `RenderOptions` passed to rendering methods.
capabilities.title: Customize rendering with options

capabilities.text: Use per-symbology options types like `Code128Options`, `Code39Options`, `Ean13Options`, and `QrOptions` to set encoding modes, check digits, and error correction.
capabilities.title: Configure symbology-specific options

capabilities.text: Implement or use built-in `Renderer` subclasses (`SvgRenderer`, `PngRenderer`, `PdfRenderer`) and pass them to `Barcode.render()`.
capabilities.title: Support custom renderers

capabilities.text: Raise specific exceptions like `BarcodeError`, `EncodingError`, `RenderingError`, and `SymbologyNotFoundError` for robust error handling.
capabilities.title: Handle errors with typed exceptions

limitations.text: PDF rendering is not implemented; `Barcode.to_pdf()` and `PdfRenderer.render()` raise `NotImplementedError`.
The library only generates barcodes and does not read or decode existing barcode images.
ECI normalization and validation are not implemented despite `EncodeOptions` exposing an `eci_assignment_number` field.
GS1 data parsing and validation are not implemented despite `EncodeOptions` exposing a `gs1_enabled` field.

problems_solved.text: Provides a pure-Python, dependency-light way to generate multiple barcode symbologies with deterministic output.
Enables rendering barcodes to SVG and PNG formats with configurable options using a consistent API.
Supports both dedicated helper functions and a generic `generate()` entry point for flexible symbology selection.
Offers fine-grained control over rendering through `RenderOptions` and custom `Renderer` subclasses.

product_summary.text: Aspose.BarCode FOSS for Python is a pure-Python, MIT-licensed library for generating deterministic, standards-compliant linear and 2D barcodes.

workflows.name: Generate and render a Code 128 barcode
workflows.text: Call `code128()` with payload data, then invoke `to_svg()` or `to_png()` to produce output.

workflows.name: Generate a QR Code with custom options
workflows.text: Use `qr()` with payload and `QrOptions` specifying error correction level and encoding mode, then render to PNG.

workflows.name: Encode a Code 39 barcode with check digit
workflows.text: Call `code39()` with payload and `Code39Options(add_check_digit=True)` to include a modulo-43 check character.

workflows.name: Select symbology by name via generic entry point
workflows.text: Invoke `generate(symbology, data)` with a canonical or alias symbology name and payload to produce a barcode.

workflows.name: Render with custom options
workflows.text: Pass `RenderOptions` to `to_svg()` or `to_png()` to control scale, DPI, module width, text display, and colors.

workflows.name: Render using a specific Renderer instance
workflows.text: Instantiate a `Renderer` subclass like `SvgRenderer`, pass it to `Barcode.render()` with `RenderOptions`, and extract rendered data.
